# Error-Handling Requirements Checklist: ART-008 slice 2 — Artifact Freshness

**Purpose**: Validate that the failure, recovery, and reporting requirements are
complete, unambiguous, internally consistent, and consistent with the shipped
ART-007 contracts this slice reuses
**Created**: 2026-08-24
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command. It
tests the *requirements*, not the implementation: every item asks whether
something is written down well, never whether code behaves.

## Scoping

The workflow prompt supplied the focus areas directly, so the three contextual
clarifying questions were resolved from it rather than asked:

- **Q1 Scope breadth** → Failure semantics of the regeneration/refresh sequence
  and its interaction with the shipped ART-007 create-or-refresh and Phase 7
  sweep contracts. Slice 1 sweep internals are out of scope (spec §Out of Scope).
- **Q2 Depth** → Standard, weighted toward the four focus bullets.
- **Q3 Audience/timing** → Reviewer, at the pre-implementation gate.

## Requirement Completeness — Failure Modes

- [x] CHK001 - Are requirements defined for every distinguishable regeneration
  shortfall (single page, whole set, unreportable dispatch)? [Completeness,
  Spec §FR-023, §FR-024, §FR-037]
- [x] CHK002 - Does the spec define what happens to the **pre-existing stale
  file** of a selected page whose regeneration returns `gap`? Re-authoring is
  whole-file only (§FR-011), the removal diff explicitly refuses to remove a
  gapped page (§FR-012a), and the reused on-disk verification deletes only
  pages *written this run*
  (`speckit-pro/skills/speckit-autopilot/references/phase-execution.md:936`), so
  the pre-amendment file survives with no requirement naming that state.
  [Gap, closed by FR-012b]
- [x] CHK003 - Are requirements defined for a **failed push of the FR-039 record
  commit** that state whether the condition is recoverable? §FR-039 asserts
  recovery "on the next refresh that reaches this step", but §FR-036 states no
  later sweep refreshes once the regeneration commit has landed. [Conflict, closed by FR-039]
- [x] CHK004 - Does §FR-019a's push-failure outcome carry the **non-repair
  statement and the manual resume path** that §FR-036 mandates for the
  structurally identical refresh failure? §FR-019a names only the unpushed sha.
  [Gap, closed by FR-019a]
- [x] CHK005 - Are requirements defined for an unusable freshness observation
  (a gather that failed) that keep it from blocking the run? [Completeness,
  Spec §FR-004a, §FR-023]
- [x] CHK006 - Are requirements defined for the case where no draft pull request
  exists at refresh time? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-034]
- [x] CHK007 - Are requirements defined for a whole-set regeneration failure
  that still oblige the description refresh to run? [Completeness, Spec §FR-037]

## Requirement Clarity — Failure Semantics

- [x] CHK008 - Does §FR-034 assign the `skipped` status **exactly one**
  behavior at the refresh call site? The shipped terminal-step table assigns it
  two branches ("Refresh the recorded pull request when the tool can be reached;
  when it cannot, report through the could-not-be-opened path",
  `phase-execution.md:1183-1187`), while §FR-034 states one and simultaneously
  claims each status takes "the behavior the ART-007 contract already assigns
  it". [Ambiguity, closed by FR-034a]
- [x] CHK009 - Is §FR-034's `no_record` behavior unambiguous about **creation**?
  It imports the shipped fallthrough, whose terminal branch is "create or
  refresh" (`phase-execution.md:1181`), into a slice whose only stated action is
  a refresh (§FR-014) and whose own sentence says "No status opens a second
  pull request" — which does not forbid a first. [Ambiguity, closed by FR-034a]
- [x] CHK010 - Does §FR-036 name a **per-status** manual resume path? The
  shipped contract requires one per discrepancy class because "the four have
  different fixes and one shared path would send an operator to the wrong
  repair" (`phase-execution.md:1345-1347`); §FR-036 names one generic path
  ("refresh the pull-request description directly"), which is not actionable for
  `pr_closed` or `pr_missing`. [Conflict, closed by FR-036]
- [x] CHK011 - Is "newer" defined without reliance on timestamps or sha string
  comparison? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004a, §FR-008]
- [x] CHK012 - Is the boundary between `no_pages` and `stale` for an
  uncommitted-but-populated directory stated explicitly? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007,
  §FR-007a]
- [x] CHK013 - Is the verdict set closed, with a stated precedence order?
  [Clarity, Spec §FR-005]
- [x] CHK014 - Is `undeterminable`'s effect on the stop-or-proceed decision
  stated in both directions rather than only as "does not stop"? [Clarity,
  Spec §FR-005a]

## Requirement Consistency — Cross-Requirement Conflicts

- [x] CHK015 - Do §FR-038 and §FR-018 agree on whether a **gapped** run is
  repaired by a later run? §FR-038 states the join "repairs an interrupted run,
  never a gapped one" and that "no later run re-attempts" a gap, but §FR-018
  takes no commit when regeneration produced no change, so a whole-set gap
  (§FR-037) leaves the join reading `stale` and the next run *does* re-attempt.
  [Conflict, closed by FR-038]
- [x] CHK016 - Is SC-001's "Zero pages are older than the newest amendment"
  consistent with the fail-open per-page gap that §FR-023 and §FR-012a permit?
  [Conflict, closed by SC-001 and FR-012b]
- [x] CHK017 - Does any requirement **scope** the shipped closed enumeration
  "Every other stop aborts before the reply point and posts none: … and a failed
  push" (`phase-execution.md:1822-1826`)? §FR-019a adds a second, leg-dependent
  failed push that the shipped sentence would misclassify. §FR-027 and §FR-033b
  scope other shipped sentences; nothing scopes this one.
  [Gap, closed by FR-015b]
- [x] CHK018 - Does any requirement scope the shipped run-ending condition list
  "a failed push" (`phase-execution.md:1310-1317`), which §FR-017 makes
  **non**-run-ending on the leg that amended nothing? [Gap, closed by FR-015b]
- [x] CHK019 - Are the three commit shapes kept mutually exclusive, with an
  explicit statement that none absorbs another? [Consistency, Spec §FR-018,
  §FR-019, §FR-020, §FR-039]
- [x] CHK020 - Is the single-writer rule for the `Draft PR` row consistent with
  §FR-039's requirement that the slice supply the commit carrying that write?
  [Consistency, Spec §FR-022, §FR-039]
- [x] CHK021 - Do §FR-021 and §FR-035 agree that a refresh failure is not a page
  failure and therefore does not enter the three-sink path? [Consistency,
  Spec §FR-021, §FR-035]

## Scenario Coverage — The Three Legs

- [x] CHK022 - Are requirements defined for the amended leg that fix the
  sequence order and the stop? [Coverage, Spec §FR-015]
- [x] CHK023 - Are requirements defined for the clean-sweep-stale leg that
  forbid converting a proceed into a stop? [Coverage, Spec §FR-017]
- [x] CHK024 - Are requirements defined for the leg that handles no comment at
  all, so the recovery case is reachable? [Coverage, Spec §FR-016]
- [x] CHK025 - Are requirements defined for the legs the entry gate stops, and
  is the resulting deferred repair stated rather than left implied? [Coverage,
  Spec §FR-016, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK026 - Is the **ordering of the reply point relative to the regeneration
  sequence** specified? Slice 1 posts replies "after every bookkeeping commit
  this run takes has landed" (`phase-execution.md:1812-1814`); the regeneration
  and record commits (§FR-018, §FR-039) are not bookkeeping commits (§FR-020),
  so nothing fixes whether replies precede or follow them. [Gap, closed by FR-015a]
- [x] CHK027 - Are requirements defined for a run that died between amending and
  regenerating, and is the recovery bounded to one subsequent run? [Recovery,
  Spec §FR-007a, §SC-003]

- [x] CHK032 - Are the **severity and repairability differences** between a

## Second Pass — Gaps The Remediation Itself Opened

- [x] CHK043 - Does FR-012b's deletion interact safely with FR-018's
  change-gated commit? First-pass FR-012b deleted the superseded file behind
  every gap. On a whole-set gap that made no difference, but a **deselection
  removal landing alone** still moved the directory, so FR-018 took a commit,
  the join read `current`, and every gapped page was stranded permanently
  stale. Closed by scoping FR-012b to a run that generated at least one page
  and by requiring FR-037 to leave the directory entirely unmoved, deselection
  removal included. [Conflict, closed by FR-037]
- [x] CHK044 - Is the interaction between FR-015a's placement and slice 1's
  **post-publication redaction stop** specified? That stop fires "once every
  commit is pushed and every reply is posted", which FR-015a now places before
  the regeneration sequence, so nothing says whether a run carrying a redaction
  event regenerates first or stops first. FR-016 says freshness is evaluated on
  every leg the sweep reaches; the redaction stop is not named as a leg either
  way. [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-015a, §FR-016] [Gap, closed by FR-015d]

## Remediation Log

| Item(s) | Root defect | Requirement change |
|---|---|---|
| CHK002, CHK016, CHK036 | A per-page `gap` left the superseded pre-amendment file on disk. No shipped sentence governs it, and the description's gap row would contradict a complete-looking page beside it. | **New FR-012b**: delete the superseded file behind a per-page gap, report it inside that page's `gap` outcome, and exclude the whole-set gap. **SC-001** gains the explicit exception clause. |
| CHK015, CHK032 | FR-038's blanket "no later run re-attempts them" was false for a whole-set gap, which takes no commit under FR-018 and is therefore retried. | **FR-038** rewritten to key repairability on whether the artifacts commit was taken, never on the shape of the shortfall. |
| CHK043 | The first-pass fix let a lone deselection removal take the commit on a run that generated nothing. | **FR-037** now requires the whole-set path to leave the directory entirely unmoved, withholding the deselection removal too. |
| CHK004 | FR-019a named only the unpushed sha, though its condition is as unrecoverable as FR-036's. | **FR-019a** gains the non-repair statement and a two-step manual resume path. |
| CHK003 | FR-039 promised the `Draft PR` row repairs itself "on the next refresh that reaches this step", which FR-036 establishes never happens. | **FR-039**'s recovery claim replaced with the reachable truth and an operator resume path. |
| CHK008, CHK009 | FR-034 claimed verbatim reuse while stating one of `skipped`'s two branches, and imported a create-capable `no_record` fallthrough. | **New FR-034a**: both statuses are unreachable here by construction, and neither may be implemented as a fallthrough to creation. |
| CHK010 | FR-036 collapsed four different repairs into one generic resume path. | **FR-036** now binds the per-status path the shipped gate already requires. |
| CHK017, CHK018, CHK026 | Two shipped closed enumerations name "a failed push"; FR-019a adds a second push whose stop is leg-dependent and post-reply. The reply point's position relative to regeneration was unstated. | **New FR-015a** fixes the sequence after the reply point; **new FR-015b** scopes both enumerations by the added-sentence technique FR-033b uses. A second pass tightened FR-015b: the reply-point sentence is an exhaustive dichotomy, so excluding the new push from "a failed push" is not enough on its own and the added sentence must also place FR-019a's amended-leg stop on the after-reply-point side. |

## Notes

- CHK044 was closed by consensus (2/2 regenerate-first, recorded as FR-015d).
  Its original framing follows: it was a genuine interaction question with
  no precedent to settle it, and it goes to consensus rather than being decided
  here.
- **Two fixed items also go to consensus**, under the routing rules rather than
  because the fix is doubted:
  - **CHK002/CHK016/CHK036 (FR-012b, and FR-037's withheld removal that rides
    with it).** Deleting the superseded file and keeping-it-while-reporting-it
    were both defensible before one was chosen. The choice is destructive and
    changes what lands in the repository, so it is surfaced rather than settled
    silently. Routed `[codebase, spec]`.
  - **CHK008 (FR-034a's `skipped` branch).** Flagged mechanically: the status it
    governs classifies an unauthenticated tool among its four causes, and the
    routing rule on security keywords is unconditional. Confidence in the fix is
    high; the flag is procedural. Routed `[security]`.
- All evidence is repo-local. Line citations were verified against
  `speckit-pro/skills/speckit-autopilot/references/phase-execution.md` and its
  Codex mirror rather than taken from the plan's existing cites, and two plan
  citations were corrected as a result.
